keyVerseText: Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached in the whole world, there shall also this, that this woman hath done, be told for a memorial of her.
rootMeaning: The root of μνημόσυνον (mnēmósynon) comes from the verb μνημονεύω (mnēmoneúō), which means to make mention of, be mindful, or remember. This root emphasizes active remembrance or mindful recollection, going beyond a mere passive memory to include the intentional act of recalling or rehearsing. The etymology highlights that μνημόσυνον is not just a simple memorial but a conscious reminder or record that preserves memory in a purposeful way.
usageInScripture: The word μνημόσυνον appears only three times in the New Testament, consistently translated as "a memorial." This consistency suggests a focused usage denoting something set apart to preserve the memory of a person, event, or deed in a lasting way. Its use in the New Testament reflects the Old Testament background where it frequently corresponds to Hebrew terms for remembrance, underscoring its role as a tangible or spoken reminder that keeps a spiritual truth or significant act alive within the community of faith.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, μνημόσυνον reminds believers that memory in Scripture is not merely historical but deeply spiritual and covenantal. It calls the church to intentional remembrance of God's actions and faithfulness, ensuring that key events and teachings are not forgotten but continually honored. This word points to the vital role of memorials in nurturing faith and obedience, as remembering God's work strengthens trust and worship. It also reflects the biblical principle that God is mindful of His people and their deeds, encouraging believers to live in a way worthy of being remembered before Him. Ultimately, μνημόσυνον helps believers see that memory is an act of faithfulness, linking past divine interventions to present trust and future hope.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 26:13, Jesus declares that the woman's act will be told "for a memorial of her" wherever the gospel is preached worldwide. Here, μνημόσυνον conveys that her deed will serve as a lasting, mindful reminder to all generations of the gospel's power and the value of sacrificial worship. This word enriches the verse by emphasizing that her act is not only remembered but honored as a meaningful testimony that will inspire faith and devotion wherever the good news is proclaimed.
